newsitem.title: UK: Business "angels" back more UK small firms in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Business "angels" back more UK small firms in 1996.

text.p: "Business "angels" who provide capital to small and start-up businesses provided 38 percent more finance in the year to end-June 1996 than in the same 1994/1995 period, British Venture Capital Association said.
The BVCA said in a report that some 388 business angels invested over 22 million stg in 212 companies, up from 16 million stg in 173 companies in the year previously.
Total investment was estimated to top 45 million stg because some of the support was part of larger financial packages.
The BVCA said the business angels provided a vital service filling the "equity gap" where small businesses find it difficult to raise relatively small amounts of capital.
A breakdown of the survey, conducted by the University of Southampton, showed 49 percent of all investments, or 45 percent of the total amount invested, were in early stage companies.
Some 39 percent of the investments were in expansion stage companies, accounting for 31 percent of the total amount.
Industry sectors receiving the most backing were support services, including software companies, engineering and leisure firms.
High technology companies, the traditional area for venture capital finance, attracted 6.0 million stg from 153 backers. -- Caroline Allen, London newsroom +44 171 542 6414
